doc.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

title: Billie Holiday and Joachim-Ernst Berendt's remark
summary: She prefers instrumentalists; Berendt told her she would need to live like Billie Holiday, which she rejected.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Is it safe to say you’ve been influenced more by horn players than singers?

Yeah. Much more by instruments than singers. Much more. And then I heard Billie Holiday and of course I adored her. Billie Holiday. She was already dead but I heard her on the record. And I adored her but I couldn’t relate to this thing that there was so much sadness in her, and it became a very one thing trip. You know she wouldn’t improvise much, she wouldn’t — it was all about just her voice expressing the experiences in her life. And that was too heavy for me. And then Joachim-Ernst Berendt, you know, the Pope of Europe, the Jazz Pope of Europe, said after the big Frankfurt Festival where I had sang and he was in the audience, and he came up to me and said, “It was really beautiful, but unless you live a life like Billie Holiday you’re not going to reach that kind of expression in your singing.” And that’s when I woke up and I said, “What? He wants me to be a prostitute? He wants me to go on drugs? He wants me to do this and this?”

Yeah. He came over here when we did for George Wein the big festival at the Avery Fisher Hall on Lincoln Center. He made all the announcements for the orchestra. There was an orchestra you know. My daughter danced. But when he said that to me I said, no. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
